name: Edinburgh
tagline: Historic Charm, World-Class Festivals, and Scottish Grit
description: Edinburgh pairs stunning medieval and Georgian architecture with a thriving cultural scene anchored by the world-famous Fringe Festival. As Scotland's capital, it offers excellent healthcare through the NHS, walkable neighborhoods, and easy access to the Highlands. While weather can be grey and costs are higher than much of Scotland, Edinburgh remains more affordable than London and rewards residents with a uniquely literary, artistic quality of life.

quickFacts.visa: 6-month visitor visa for US citizens. No dedicated retirement visa. Investor visa requires £2M+ investment. Most retirees cycle tourist visas or explore ancestry-based routes if eligible.
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of the safest cities in the UK
quickFacts.climate: Maritime continental with cool summers and cold, windy winters

housing.description: Small 1-bedroom or studio in Gorgie, Dalry, or Leith — functional, not central

dining.description: Mostly home cooking plus an occasional cheap meal out

healthcare.description: IHS plus a minimal cash/dental buffer

transportation.description: Lothian Buses Ridacard (£74) plus walking; no car

1M.lifestyle: A small one-bedroom or studio in Gorgie, Dalry, or Leith, getting around on a Lothian Buses Ridacard and on foot. Most meals are cooked at home with the odd cheap meal out, and NHS access comes via the Immigration Health Surcharge. Winter heating is a real line in the budget and dining out is limited, but the free museums, Arthur's Seat, and the August festival atmosphere make lean life here unusually rich.

housing.description: Solid 1-bedroom in Leith, Marchmont, or Bruntsfield

healthcare.description: IHS plus a basic private top-up (~AXA entry)

transportation.description: Ridacard plus occasional taxis and ScotRail

2M.lifestyle: A solid one-bedroom in Leith, Marchmont, or Bruntsfield, with regular casual dining and a mid-tier private layer on top of NHS access. The Ridacard plus occasional taxis and ScotRail cover the city and beyond, and there is room for theatre, concerts, and a gym. Comfortable, walkable Edinburgh living.

housing.description: Well-appointed 1-bedroom in Stockbridge, the New Town edge, or central Leith

transportation.description: Ridacard plus regular taxis and intercity rail

3M.lifestyle: A well-appointed one-bedroom in Stockbridge, the New Town edge, or central Leith. Dining out is frequent, comprehensive private cover (Bupa/AXA) sits on top of the NHS, and the Ridacard plus regular taxis and intercity rail cover travel. Festivals, theatre, and leisure are routine, with genuine monthly margin — affluent life in a beautiful, compact capital.

housing.description: Premium 2-bedroom in the New Town or a prime central flat

healthcare.description: IHS plus a premium private plan, low excess

transportation.description: Ridacard plus frequent taxis and a part-time car/hire for Highland trips

5M.lifestyle: A premium two-bedroom in the New Town or a prime central flat, with a weekly cleaner. Dining is regular and fine, a premium private plan removes friction, and the Ridacard plus frequent taxis and a part-time car or hire cover Highland trips. Culture, clubs, and premium festival seats fill out an upper-affluent life.

housing.description: Grand Georgian townhouse in Heriot Row or the New Town, or a country property on the outskirts

dining.description: The city's best tables plus private-chef occasions

healthcare.description: IHS plus premium concierge private care

transportation.description: Owned car plus driver hire, first-class rail, taxis

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper several times a week (~50 hrs/mo @ ~£16.5/hr)

10M.lifestyle: A grand Georgian townhouse in Heriot Row or the New Town, or a country property on the outskirts, kept by a housekeeper several times a week. Dining runs to the city's best tables and private-chef occasions, health cover pairs NHS access with premium concierge private care, and an owned car with driver hire plus first-class rail handle travel. The discretionary budget funds festival hospitality, art, memberships, and constant travel — the top of Edinburgh's market, where a grand townhouse or a Highland retreat fills the margin.
